references.text: Jesus confirms that the Son can do nothing on his own, but only what he sees the Father doing, emphasizing that all power and action come from God.
Jesus expresses that without him people can do nothing, a direct parallel to the claim that the blind man's actions could not have happened unless he was from God.
Nicodemus acknowledges that Jesus has come from God because no one can perform the signs he does, reflecting the logic in John 9:33.
Jesus asks that people believe in the "works" even if they do not believe in him, so that they may know and understand that the Father is in him and he is in the Father.
Jesus explains that the words he speaks and the works he does are not from himself, but the Father who dwells in him performs his own works.
